summary: Right now, the team is juggling urgent email access fixes with two major initiatives: finalizing the knowledge website redesign and executing the global marketing strategy for Asia Start and Intelligent China.
summaryDetail: The most immediate priority is resolving the Outlook account lockout that is blocking team communication—everyone must re-login and update passwords on all devices, and confirm with JSB that the backend lock is cleared. In parallel, the knowledge website redesign is at a critical decision point: Joseph needs to share his HTML design, and a 30-minute feedback meeting must be scheduled to merge the two homepage concepts, with Joker implementing changes. On the marketing front, the strategy to prioritize Asia Start and Intelligent China is moving forward: Joseph is drafting the target areas and prompts, while the team audits conversion tracking and analyzes participant profiles; US programs, including Berkeley, are on hold. Looking ahead, several deliverables are due by September 30: Julie must update the CKGSB-IE report promotion and share SIP report info, Joseph must finalize the Asia Start video logo and share the Intelligent China webpage, and LIU Xuan must provide information to Swisscham and save the Tech in Asia participant list. Additionally, the team needs to send a combined thank-you and follow-up email to Tech in Asia participants, with touch points created by Ben and Jay.

meetings.title: Knowledge Website Redesign Review
meetings.summary: The team reviewed two homepage design concepts for the knowledge website, comparing them to the current version and discussing layout, menu structure, and content display. They agreed to combine elements from both designs and schedule a follow-up meeting for detailed feedback.

meetings.title: CKGSB Global Marketing Strategy Meeting
meetings.summary: The team discussed prioritizing China-based programs (Asia Star and Intelligent China) for SEO and marketing, with a focus on understanding target audience and conversion tracking. They agreed to draft a strategy, audit existing tracking, and consider US programs as secondary.

decisions.text: Remove the videos panel and disperse videos by topic instead of having a separate category.
Keep the two-menu structure (Knowledge and School) at the top, with the Knowledge menu centered.
Incorporate more articles on the homepage, similar to Joseph's editorial-style layout.
Bring indices (BCI, BSI) more prominently onto the knowledge homepage.

Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China programs for marketing efforts.
Put US partnership programs on hold initially, but consider Berkeley as a third priority.
Focus on China-based programs due to higher demand from overseas executives.
Send one combined email with appreciation and program information to Tech in Asia participants, instead of separate thank-you and follow-up emails
